cards.statement: Vue 2's official End of Life date is December 31, 2023.
cards.explanation: Vue's FAQ records December 31, 2023 as Vue 2's End of Life.
cards.volatilityNote: The FAQ's support-status wording may be revised.

source.title: Frequently Asked Questions: Is Vue 2 Still Supported?

cards.statement: In the Options API, Vue uses the Composition API as the underlying implementation.
cards.explanation: The Options API uses the same underlying system that powers the Composition API.

cards.statement: Vue's documentation recommends Composition API with Single-File Components for full applications.
cards.explanation: Vue's guide recommends this combination for full applications, where flexible logic organization helps.

cards.statement: createApp receives a component definition to use as the application's root.
cards.explanation: createApp uses its first argument as the root component definition.

cards.statement: Calling app.use() again with the same plugin repeats that plugin's installation.
cards.explanation: An application installs a given plugin once, even when app.use() receives it repeatedly.
cards.misconception: Repeating app.use() repeats installation.

cards.statement: app.mount() returns the application instance for further configuration.
cards.explanation: app.mount() returns the root component instance.
cards.misconception: app.mount() returns the app.

cards.statement: Each Vue application on a page has its own configuration and global assets.
cards.explanation: Separate application instances keep their configuration and global registrations scoped to their own app.

source.title: Creating a Vue Application: Multiple Application Instances

cards.statement: The browser compiles a Single-File Component's template when the component first mounts.
cards.explanation: @vue/compiler-sfc pre-compiles SFCs into standard ES modules as part of the build.
cards.misconception: The browser compiles SFC templates at mount time.

cards.statement: create-vue scaffolds new Vue projects around a webpack build.
cards.explanation: create-vue scaffolds a Vue project that uses Vite.
cards.misconception: create-vue uses webpack.

cards.statement: Hand-written render functions receive the same compile-time optimizations as Vue templates.
cards.explanation: Vue's compiler optimizes templates through static analysis. Hand-written render functions receive fewer compile-time optimizations.
cards.misconception: Manual render functions get equivalent optimizations.

source.title: Rendering Mechanism: Templates vs. Render Functions

cards.statement: Vue 3 supports IE11 when a build supplies polyfills for its JavaScript features.
cards.explanation: Vue 3 needs native ES2016 browser support. Its required features include ones that IE11 polyfills cannot supply.
cards.misconception: Polyfills make IE11 compatible.

cards.statement: Text interpolation displays an HTML string as text in the rendered page.
cards.explanation: Vue displays interpolated strings as plain text, so HTML markup appears as text.

cards.statement: Vue evaluates template bindings inside content inserted by v-html.
cards.explanation: v-html inserts HTML content. Vue ignores template bindings inside that content.
cards.misconception: v-html compiles nested bindings.

cards.statement: `:id="null"` removes the id attribute from the rendered element.
cards.explanation: Vue removes a bound attribute when its value is null or undefined.

cards.statement: Vue omits a bound disabled attribute when its value is an empty string.
cards.explanation: Vue includes a Boolean attribute bound to an empty string.
cards.misconception: Empty strings omit Boolean attributes.

cards.statement: In Vue 3.4 and later, `:title` binds the title attribute to the title variable.
cards.explanation: The same-name shorthand expands :title to :title="title".

cards.statement: A text interpolation accepts an if statement to choose the displayed value.
cards.explanation: A text interpolation accepts an expression, such as a ternary; an if statement is invalid there.
cards.misconception: Interpolations accept statements.

cards.statement: Template expressions directly access custom properties attached to window.
cards.explanation: Vue restricts template globals to a predefined list. app.config.globalProperties exposes additional globals.
cards.misconception: Custom window globals enter template scope.

cards.statement: `:[field]="value"` lets Vue choose the attribute name from the string stored in field.
cards.explanation: Vue evaluates the bracketed expression to determine the binding's argument.

cards.statement: `:class="{ selected: active }"` includes selected when active is truthy.
cards.explanation: Vue uses each object's value to decide whether its corresponding class appears.

source.title: Class and Style Bindings: Binding to Objects

cards.statement: A :class binding replaces the classes declared in a plain class attribute.
cards.explanation: Vue combines bound classes with the element's plain class attribute.
cards.misconception: Bound classes replace static classes.

source.title: Class and Style Bindings: Binding to Objects

cards.statement: Vue treats objects in a :style array as fallback alternatives for an element.
cards.explanation: Vue merges the objects in a :style array and applies the combined styles.
cards.misconception: Style arrays choose fallback objects.

source.title: Class and Style Bindings: Style Arrays

cards.statement: A `<template>` element with v-if groups several elements under one condition.
cards.explanation: Vue uses <template v-if> as an invisible wrapper for a conditional group.

cards.statement: v-show removes a hidden element from the DOM until its condition becomes truthy.
cards.explanation: v-show keeps the element in the DOM and controls visibility through its display style.
cards.misconception: v-show detaches hidden elements.

cards.statement: v-for sorts an object's property names alphabetically before rendering its values.
cards.explanation: An object v-for follows Object.values() order rather than sorting property names.
cards.misconception: Object loops alphabetize properties.

source.title: List Rendering: v-for with an Object

cards.statement: `v-for="n in 4"` starts n at 1 when rendering its integer range.
cards.explanation: Vue's integer-range v-for produces values from 1 through the supplied integer.

source.title: List Rendering: v-for with a Range

cards.statement: On an element with v-if and v-for, Vue evaluates v-for before v-if.
cards.explanation: Vue evaluates v-if before v-for on the same element.
cards.misconception: v-for runs before v-if.

cards.statement: By default, Vue patches v-for list elements in place instead of moving them when the data order changes.
cards.explanation: Without keys, Vue keeps each DOM element at its index and updates its content: efficient, but unsafe when items hold child component state or form input values.

source.title: List Rendering: Maintaining State with key

cards.statement: In a `<template v-for>`, the key attribute belongs on the child elements inside the template.
cards.explanation: Vue expects the key of a <template v-for> on the <template> tag itself, because the template is the unit that repeats for each item.
cards.misconception: Template loop keys belong on the children, as in Vue 2.

source.title: List Rendering: Maintaining State with key

cards.statement: A component rendered by v-for automatically receives the loop item as a prop.
cards.explanation: A component in v-for receives loop data through explicitly bound props.
cards.misconception: Component loops inject item props.

source.title: List Rendering: v-for with a Component

cards.statement: Replacing a list's array lets Vue reuse existing DOM elements for overlapping items.
cards.explanation: Vue seeks to reuse matching DOM elements when a replacement array contains overlapping objects.

cards.statement: Vue automatically passes the native DOM event to a method handler bound as `@click="save"`.
cards.explanation: Vue supplies the triggering native event as the argument to a DOM method handler.

cards.statement: Vue treats `@click="save()"` as a method handler because it calls a component function.
cards.explanation: Vue classifies a call expression such as save() as an inline handler.
cards.misconception: A function call is a method handler.

source.title: Event Handling: Method vs. Inline Detection

cards.statement: Vue gives `@click.prevent.self` and `@click.self.prevent` identical behavior for child clicks.
cards.explanation: Vue applies modifiers in order; putting .self first skips .prevent for child clicks.
cards.misconception: Modifier order has identical effects.

cards.statement: `@click.ctrl.exact` runs its handler when Ctrl is the sole pressed system modifier.
cards.explanation: The .exact modifier excludes clicks with additional system modifier keys pressed.

cards.statement: The .passive modifier lets a handler cancel the event's default browser action.
cards.explanation: A passive listener commits to leaving the default action uncanceled, so .passive conflicts with .prevent.
cards.misconception: Passive listeners allow cancellation.

cards.statement: v-model uses the bound JavaScript state as the initial source of a form field's value.
cards.explanation: Vue initializes v-model from JavaScript state, ignoring initial value, checked and selected attributes.

cards.statement: v-model updates its bound text value during an input method editor's composition phase.
cards.explanation: v-model defers text updates during IME composition until composition ends.
cards.misconception: IME composition updates v-model immediately.

cards.statement: Checkboxes sharing an array through v-model put the checked boxes' values into that array.
cards.explanation: The shared v-model array contains the values of the currently checked boxes.

cards.statement: On a text input, v-model.lazy synchronizes the bound state after change events.
cards.explanation: The .lazy modifier makes text-input v-model listen for change events.

cards.statement: v-model converts an object bound to a select option's :value into a string upon selection.
cards.explanation: A selected option's object binding remains an object in the v-model state.
cards.misconception: Select values become strings.

cards.statement: JavaScript code reads and changes a ref's stored value through its `.value` property.
cards.explanation: Vue tracks reads and writes of `.value` to connect the ref to dependent effects.

cards.statement: By default, Vue makes an object held in a ref's `.value` deeply reactive.
cards.explanation: Vue makes an object's nested state reactive when it becomes the value of a ref.

cards.statement: Mutating the plain object passed to reactive() triggers updates through its returned proxy.
cards.explanation: Vue observes mutations through the proxy returned by reactive(), rather than changes made directly to the original object.
cards.misconception: reactive() makes the original object reactive in place.

cards.statement: A reactive array returns a stored ref's inner value when JavaScript reads that array element.
cards.explanation: JavaScript receives the ref itself from a reactive array element; use `.value` to read its inner value.
cards.misconception: Reactive arrays unwrap refs when their elements are read.

cards.statement: Destructuring a number from a reactive object preserves its connection to the object's state.
cards.explanation: A destructured primitive is a separate value; reading or assigning it bypasses the reactive object's property access.
cards.misconception: Destructured primitives stay linked to reactive properties.

cards.statement: After a reactive state change, awaiting nextTick() waits for Vue to finish the pending DOM update.
cards.explanation: Vue batches DOM updates; nextTick() resolves after that update flush completes.

cards.statement: In Vue 3.3 and later, toValue() preserves a getter function as its returned value.
cards.explanation: toValue() invokes a getter and returns its result.
cards.misconception: toValue() treats a getter like an ordinary value.

cards.statement: Vue's documentation recommends a plain object of refs as a composable's return value.
cards.explanation: A composable returning a plain object of refs lets callers destructure the refs while keeping their reactive state connections.

cards.statement: A ref created inside a composable call shares its state with other callers of that composable.
cards.explanation: A ref created inside the composable function belongs to that invocation. Separate calls create separate refs.
cards.misconception: Composables automatically share locally created state across callers.

cards.statement: A component re-render refreshes the timestamp returned by `computed(() => Date.now())`.
cards.explanation: A computed getter that reads Date.now() stays cached because the clock supplies no reactive dependency.
cards.misconception: Component re-renders invalidate computed values automatically.

cards.statement: In Vue 3.4 and later, a computed getter receives its previously returned result as its first argument.
cards.explanation: A computed getter's previous-value argument contains its earlier result, rather than an old dependency value.

cards.statement: With `const obj = reactive({ count: 0 })`, `watch(obj.count, callback)` tracks later count changes.
cards.explanation: Pass `() => obj.count` as the source. Passing obj.count supplies a number, which watch() cannot track.
cards.misconception: watch() tracks a reactive property's later values when given its current primitive value.

cards.statement: Passing a reactive object directly to watch() enables deep observation by default.
cards.explanation: Nested property mutations trigger the callback when the reactive object itself is the watch source.

cards.statement: In Vue 3.5 and later, a numeric watch() `deep` option sets the maximum depth Vue traverses.
cards.explanation: A numeric deep value limits how far watch() traverses nested state to collect dependencies.

cards.statement: A watch() callback with `immediate: true` receives the initial source value as its old value on its first run.
cards.explanation: With immediate: true, the first callback's old value is undefined because no earlier watched value exists.
cards.misconception: An immediate watcher's initial old value equals its initial source value.

cards.statement: An async watchEffect() tracks reactive properties first accessed after its first await.
cards.explanation: watchEffect() collects dependencies during its synchronous execution, before the first await.
cards.misconception: watchEffect() continues collecting new dependencies after asynchronous suspension.

cards.statement: In Vue 3.5 and later, onWatcherCleanup() requires registration during the watcher's synchronous execution.
cards.explanation: Register cleanup inside the running watcher callback or effect, before awaiting asynchronous work.

cards.statement: By default, a watch() callback runs after Vue updates the owner's DOM for the current change.
cards.explanation: Vue runs the default callback before updating the owner's DOM, so it sees the earlier DOM state.
cards.misconception: Default watcher callbacks see their owner's freshly updated DOM.

cards.statement: Vue stops a watcher created inside setTimeout() when its component unmounts.
cards.explanation: A watcher created in a timer callback is detached from component ownership; stop it explicitly.
cards.misconception: Asynchronously created watchers share their component's cleanup lifecycle.

cards.statement: Vue waits for a detached root container to enter the document before calling onMounted.
cards.explanation: onMounted guarantees insertion into the parent container; it does not wait for document attachment.
cards.misconception: The mounted hook waits for the root container to join the document.

cards.statement: Vue calls a parent's onUpdated callback before the onUpdated callbacks of its updated children.
cards.explanation: A parent's onUpdated callback runs after its children's updated callbacks.
cards.misconception: Parent updated hooks precede child updated hooks.

cards.statement: Returning false from onErrorCaptured forwards the captured error to app.config.errorHandler.
cards.explanation: Returning false from onErrorCaptured stops further propagation, including the application's error handler.
cards.misconception: Returning false marks an error as unhandled.

cards.statement: Vue accepts onMounted registration inside an external function called synchronously during setup().
cards.explanation: Vue associates the hook with the component active in the synchronous setup call stack.

cards.statement: In a server-rendered app, createSSRApp makes client mounting hydrate the existing HTML.
cards.explanation: Vue uses hydration mode to connect the client application to its server-rendered DOM.

cards.statement: In a server-rendered app, renderToString() produces the rendered HTML synchronously as a plain string.
cards.explanation: renderToString() from vue/server-renderer gives a Promise that resolves to the rendered HTML, so server code awaits it.
cards.misconception: Server HTML rendering hands back its final string synchronously.

cards.statement: During SSR, Vue enables its reactivity system by default when it renders the application's HTML.
cards.explanation: Vue disables reactivity by default during SSR because server rendering has no interactive DOM updates.
cards.misconception: Server rendering tracks dependencies like client rendering.

cards.statement: During SSR, Vue runs onMounted callbacks after it produces the component's HTML.
cards.explanation: onMounted runs on the client, not during server rendering.
cards.misconception: Producing server HTML triggers the mounted hook.

cards.statement: During SSR, shared module-level state can leak one user's data into another user's request.
cards.explanation: Server requests can reuse singleton module state, letting user-specific mutations cross request boundaries.

cards.statement: In a server-rendered app on Vue 3.5 and later, useId() produces IDs stable across server and client renders.
cards.explanation: Vue keeps useId() results consistent between server rendering and client hydration.

cards.statement: Vue calls defineProps() at runtime when a component declares its props.
cards.explanation: defineProps() is a compiler macro that Vue removes when compiling <script setup>.
cards.misconception: defineProps() is a runtime function.

cards.statement: defineProps() can use a local ref's `.value` as a prop default in the same `<script setup>` block.
cards.explanation: Vue hoists defineProps() options to module scope. A local ref from <script setup> is outside that scope.
cards.misconception: Prop declarations evaluate inside the component's setup scope.

cards.statement: In Vue 3.5 and later, destructured defineProps() values track parent updates in the same `<script setup>` block.
cards.explanation: Vue rewrites accesses to destructured props as property reads, preserving their reactive connection.

cards.statement: In a runtime declaration, `defineProps({ title: String })` makes title a required prop.
cards.explanation: String only declares the value type; runtime-declared props stay optional unless their declaration specifies required: true.
cards.misconception: A constructor declaration makes the prop required.

cards.statement: `defineProps({ enabled: Boolean })` gives enabled the value false when the parent omits it.
cards.explanation: An absent Boolean prop casts to false under this declaration.

cards.statement: Vue uses a prop's declared default when its parent explicitly passes undefined.
cards.explanation: Prop defaults apply when Vue resolves the incoming value to undefined, including an explicitly supplied value.

cards.statement: A child's nested writes to an object prop change the shared object held in the parent's state.
cards.explanation: Objects are passed by reference, so Vue blocks only reassigning the prop itself. The docs advise avoiding such writes unless parent and child are tightly coupled, and emitting an event instead.

cards.statement: Vue validates a custom class prop by checking that the incoming object has matching fields.
cards.explanation: Vue checks a custom class prop with instanceof; matching fields alone do not satisfy that check.
cards.misconception: Custom class prop checks use structural field matching.

cards.statement: Vue casts bare enabled to true with `defineProps({ enabled: [String, Boolean] })`.
cards.explanation: With String before Boolean, a bare enabled attribute becomes an empty string.
cards.misconception: Boolean casting takes precedence regardless of type order.

cards.statement: A parent's local component registration automatically makes that component available in descendant templates.
cards.explanation: Local registration belongs to the declaring component. Descendants register or import their components independently.
cards.misconception: Descendants inherit locally registered components.

cards.statement: Vue exposes components imported in `<script setup>` for direct use as tags in that SFC's template.
cards.explanation: The SFC compiler resolves imported component bindings as template tags.

cards.statement: Vue bubbles a component-emitted event through the component's ancestor chain.
cards.explanation: A component event reaches listeners on its direct parent, rather than propagating through ancestor components.
cards.misconception: Component events bubble like native DOM events.

cards.statement: Declaring click in defineEmits() restricts the parent's @click listener to component-emitted events.
cards.explanation: A declared click event consumes the parent's listener, excluding native clicks from that listener.

cards.statement: Vue forwards the values following the event name in an emit() call to the parent listener.
cards.explanation: Additional emit() arguments become listener arguments in the same order.

cards.statement: In Vue 3.4 and later, changing defineModel()'s returned ref updates the parent's bound v-model value.
cards.explanation: The model ref connects child writes to the parent value bound with v-model.

cards.statement: A component accepts several v-model bindings that target distinct model arguments.
cards.explanation: Different arguments let one component bind separate model values for its parent.

cards.statement: In Vue 3.4 and later, a defineModel() default initializes an undefined parent v-model ref.
cards.explanation: A defineModel() default fills the child's model while an undefined parent ref stays undefined, creating a mismatch.
cards.misconception: A child's model default initializes the parent's ref.

cards.statement: Vue merges a parent's fallthrough class with the class on a child's single root element.
cards.explanation: The root retains its local classes alongside the inherited classes.

cards.statement: An inherited @click handler replaces the child's own @click handler on its root element.
cards.explanation: A root click invokes both the local handler and the inherited handler.
cards.misconception: An inherited listener overrides the child's root listener.

cards.statement: Vue applies fallthrough attributes to the first root element of a multi-root component.
cards.explanation: A multi-root component explicitly binds $attrs to choose the receiving element.
cards.misconception: Vue chooses the first root as the attribute target.

cards.statement: Vue exposes a fallthrough @click listener as a function at `$attrs.onClick`.
cards.explanation: $attrs uses onClick as the JavaScript key for a fallthrough click listener.

cards.statement: In `$attrs`, Vue stores a parent's fallthrough `foo-bar` attribute under the camelCase key `fooBar`.
cards.explanation: Unlike props, fallthrough attributes keep their original casing in JavaScript, so a child reads a foo-bar attribute as `$attrs['foo-bar']`.
cards.misconception: Fallthrough attribute names are camelCased in $attrs the way prop names are.

cards.statement: Vue assigns ordinary child elements between component tags to the child's first named slot.
cards.explanation: Ordinary top-level child nodes go to the default slot.
cards.misconception: Unnamed content fills the first outlet.

cards.statement: A scoped slot supports child-supplied data through the props passed to its slot outlet.
cards.explanation: The child passes slot props when invoking the parent's slot content.

cards.statement: Vue includes a named slot outlet's name attribute in the props received by that slot.
cards.explanation: Vue reserves name for slot selection and excludes it from slot props.
cards.misconception: The slot name joins the slot props.

cards.statement: A component-level v-slot supports a default scoped slot alongside named slot templates.
cards.explanation: Use an explicit template for the default scoped slot when mixing it with named slots.
cards.misconception: Component-level v-slot works beside named templates.

cards.statement: inject() chooses the nearest ancestor's value when several ancestors provide the same key.
cards.explanation: A closer provider shadows a matching key higher in the parent chain.

cards.statement: inject() returns a provided ref's inner value when a component requests that key.
cards.explanation: inject() returns the provided ref itself, preserving its reactive connection.
cards.misconception: Injection unwraps refs like template access.

cards.statement: Passing true as inject()'s third argument makes its function default run as a factory.
cards.explanation: inject() calls a function default as a factory when its third argument is true and the key has no provider.

cards.statement: Vue's documentation recommends keeping mutations of provided reactive state in the provider.
cards.explanation: Keeping provided state and its mutations together simplifies maintenance.

cards.statement: Providing readonly(count) prevents the provider from changing its original mutable count ref.
cards.explanation: The provider retains its writable original ref while injectors receive its readonly wrapper.
cards.misconception: readonly() freezes the original ref.

cards.statement: Vue runs the code in `<script setup>` separately when it creates each component instance.
cards.explanation: Vue compiles this code into the component's setup function, giving instances separate executions.

cards.statement: Vue resolves `v-focus` to a local binding named `focus` in `<script setup>`.
cards.explanation: Vue recognizes a local vFocus binding for v-focus; the variable name needs the v prefix.
cards.misconception: Local directive bindings use the bare directive name.

cards.statement: Vue exposes a `<script setup>` component's top-level bindings through a parent's template ref by default.
cards.explanation: A script setup component keeps its bindings private unless it exposes a public interface with defineExpose().
cards.misconception: Setup bindings automatically become public instance properties.

cards.statement: Vue compiles top-level await in `<script setup>` into an async setup() function.
cards.explanation: The SFC compiler makes setup asynchronous to handle the top-level awaited work.

cards.statement: In Vue 3.5 and later, a DOM ref from useTemplateRef() holds its element before Vue mounts the component.
cards.explanation: The template ref's value starts as null because Vue has yet to create the element.
cards.misconception: Template refs contain their DOM elements during setup.

cards.statement: Vue keeps a v-for template ref array in the same order as the loop's source array.
cards.explanation: Vue does not guarantee that a template ref array matches the source array's order.
cards.misconception: Template ref array positions reliably match source positions.

cards.statement: Vue passes null to a function bound as an element's template ref when that element unmounts.
cards.explanation: Use the null argument to clear the stored reference to the removed element.

cards.statement: Vue applies matching parent scoped styles to a child component's root element.
cards.explanation: The child's root carries the parent's style scope so the parent can control its layout.

cards.statement: Vue automatically adds scoped style attributes to elements rendered through v-html.
cards.explanation: Content inserted by v-html falls outside the component's scoped CSS transformation.
cards.misconception: Vue scopes HTML injected by v-html like compiled template nodes.

cards.statement: For a class panel declared in `<style module>`, `$style.panel` holds the unchanged class name panel.
cards.explanation: Vue hashes CSS Modules classes to avoid collisions, so $style.panel holds the generated class name rather than panel, which scopes the class to the current component.
cards.misconception: CSS Modules keep the source class name in $style.

cards.statement: Vue automatically compiles CSS v-bind() expressions from an SFC's style block into hashed CSS custom properties.
cards.explanation: Vue uses the generated custom property to connect the CSS value to component state.

cards.statement: Transition can animate a component's multiple root elements as one transition target.
cards.explanation: Transition accepts a component with a single root element as its transition target.
cards.misconception: A component fragment becomes one transition target.

cards.statement: A named Transition automatically uses its name prop as the prefix for its default CSS classes.
cards.explanation: The name prop replaces Vue's usual v prefix in the generated enter and leave class names.

cards.statement: TransitionGroup renders a span element around its list items by default.
cards.explanation: TransitionGroup renders no wrapper by default. Set its tag prop to create a wrapper element.
cards.misconception: TransitionGroup supplies a default span wrapper.

cards.statement: TransitionGroup requires a unique key on each element it animates in a list.
cards.explanation: Vue uses those keys to identify the individual list items through insertions, removals and order changes.

cards.statement: KeepAlive's include filter matches the imported binding name used in the parent's template.
cards.explanation: KeepAlive checks its include filter against the component's name option.
cards.misconception: Cache filters match a component's local import alias.

cards.statement: KeepAlive makes room at its max limit by evicting the cached instance accessed least recently.
cards.explanation: KeepAlive uses recent access to choose which instance to destroy when a new entry would exceed max.

cards.statement: Vue delays a kept-alive component's onActivated hook until the component is re-inserted from the cache.
cards.explanation: onActivated runs on a kept-alive component's initial mount and again every time the component is re-inserted from the cache.
cards.misconception: Activation callbacks begin only with the first restoration from the cache.

cards.statement: A component inside Teleport keeps its original logical parent for props, events and injection.
cards.explanation: Teleport relocates rendered DOM while preserving the component hierarchy used for communication.

cards.statement: In Vue 3.5 and later, Teleport's defer prop waits across future ticks for its target to appear.
cards.explanation: A deferred Teleport target must exist in the same mount or update tick; defer does not wait for a later tick.
cards.misconception: Deferred target resolution keeps waiting until the target eventually exists.

cards.statement: The experimental Suspense component can wait for a descendant's async setup() to resolve.
cards.explanation: Suspense treats a component with async setup() as an async dependency while coordinating its loading state.
cards.volatilityNote: Suspense remains experimental, and its API may change.

cards.statement: In Vue Router, loading a route through a dynamic import triggers the experimental Suspense component's pending state.
cards.explanation: Vue Router's lazy route loading does not trigger Suspense.
cards.misconception: A lazy route component is a Suspense async dependency.
cards.volatilityNote: Suspense remains experimental, and its API may change.

cards.statement: In Vue Router 5, file-based routing is part of the core package, with its Vite plugin at vue-router/vite.
cards.explanation: Vue Router 5 merged unplugin-vue-router into the core package; its plugin generates the routes from page components.
cards.volatilityNote: Names Vue Router 5; file-based routing only recently moved into the core package and may keep evolving.

cards.statement: The Vue Router documentation recommends the HTML5 history mode created with createWebHistory().
cards.explanation: createWebHistory() produces normal-looking URLs; the server needs a catch-all fallback to index.html so direct visits to deep URLs load the app.

cards.statement: In Vue Router, a component imports RouterLink from vue-router before its template can use that tag.
cards.explanation: app.use(router) registers RouterView and RouterLink globally, so templates use them without an import; a local import stays optional.
cards.misconception: Router components need a local import in each component.

cards.statement: In Vue Router, useRoute() returns a static copy of the route captured when the component's setup runs.
cards.explanation: useRoute() returns a reactive route object; the docs advise watching the specific properties you need rather than the whole route.
cards.misconception: useRoute() gives a one-time snapshot of the current route.

source.title: Vue Router and the Composition API

cards.statement: In Vue Router, navigating from /users/1 to /users/2 on one route reuses the same component instance.
cards.explanation: Rendering the same component, Vue Router keeps the instance instead of recreating it, so some of its lifecycle hooks do not run again; onBeforeRouteUpdate can react to the change.

cards.statement: In Vue Router, a child route path that starts with / resolves relative to its parent route's path.
cards.explanation: Vue Router treats a nested path starting with / as a root path, which keeps the component nesting without a nested URL.
cards.misconception: Child paths are always prefixed with the parent path.

cards.statement: In Vue Router, router.push() ignores params when its location object also includes a path.
cards.explanation: Pass a route name with params, or build the whole path yourself; query, unlike params, works alongside path.

cards.statement: In Vue Router, a beforeEnter guard on a route that redirects runs before the redirect takes place.
cards.explanation: Vue Router applies navigation guards to the redirect's target, not to the redirecting route, so a beforeEnter there has no effect.
cards.misconception: Guards on a redirecting route run before it redirects.

cards.statement: In Vue Router, returning false from a router.beforeEach() guard cancels the current navigation.
cards.explanation: If the browser URL already changed, Vue Router resets it to the from location; returning nothing or true validates the navigation instead.

cards.statement: In Vue Router, route.meta deep-merges nested objects found in the meta fields of parent and child records.
cards.explanation: route.meta is a non-recursive merge of the matched records' meta fields from parent to child; route.matched keeps each record's own meta.
cards.misconception: route.meta combines nested meta objects recursively.

cards.statement: The Vue Router documentation recommends defineAsyncComponent() for route components that load lazily.
cards.explanation: A lazy route component is a plain function that returns a dynamic import; the docs advise against using async components as route components.
cards.misconception: Lazy route components are Vue async components.

cards.statement: In Vue Router, setting `props: true` on a route passes route.params to its component as props.
cards.explanation: This boolean mode decouples the component from $route; object mode passes static props and function mode computes props from the route.

cards.statement: In Pinia, an Option Store's state option takes a plain object holding the store's initial values.
cards.explanation: state is a function that returns the initial state, which lets Pinia work on both the server and the client.
cards.misconception: Option Store state is a plain object.

cards.statement: In Pinia, a ref that a Setup Store leaves out of its returned object still becomes part of the store's state.
cards.explanation: Pinia picks up state only from the properties a Setup Store returns, so the docs say to return every state property; leaving one out breaks SSR, devtools and plugins.
cards.misconception: Every ref declared inside a Setup Store becomes store state, even when it is not returned.

cards.statement: In Pinia, defineStore() creates the store instance as soon as the module that defines it is imported.
cards.explanation: defineStore() returns a useStore function, and Pinia creates the store the first time that function is called, for example in script setup.
cards.misconception: Importing a store module instantiates the store.

cards.statement: In Pinia, storeToRefs() returns refs for a store's state and getters while skipping its actions.
cards.explanation: Destructuring the store itself breaks reactivity; actions are bound to the store, so they can be destructured from it directly.

cards.statement: In Pinia, a component changes state by assigning to a store property directly, as in store.count++.
cards.explanation: Pinia needs no mutation wrappers: code reads and writes state on the store instance, and v-model binds to a store property.

cards.statement: In Pinia, $patch() accepts a function that receives the state, which suits changes such as array pushes.
cards.explanation: The function form groups mutations that are awkward as a patch object, such as pushing to or splicing an array.

cards.statement: In Pinia, a Setup Store gets a built-in $reset() that restores its state to the initial values.
cards.explanation: Option Stores come with a built-in $reset(); in a Setup Store you write your own $reset() function and return it from the store like an action.
cards.misconception: Every store style provides $reset() automatically.

cards.statement: In Pinia, a getter that returns a function caches the result for each argument it receives.
cards.explanation: A getter that returns a function is no longer cached; each call runs the function, though the getter may cache intermediate data itself.
cards.misconception: Getters cache results per argument.

cards.statement: In Pinia, an action can be async and await API calls or other actions before it changes state.
cards.explanation: Unlike getters, actions can be asynchronous; any library that returns a Promise works, and an action can use other stores.

cards.statement: In Pinia, $subscribe() runs its callback once for a single $patch() call that changes several properties.
cards.explanation: Subscriptions trigger once after a patch, an advantage over a plain watch(); $subscribe() also accepts watch() options such as flush.

cards.statement: In Pinia, calling a useStore() function at module top level before app.use(pinia) returns a working store.
cards.explanation: useStore() needs an installed pinia instance; in a single-page app, call it after app.use(pinia), for example inside a function such as a guard.
cards.misconception: A store works before the pinia plugin is installed.

source.title: Using a store outside of a component
